-   **Rarity note:** Common species in Florida, found in areas with high leaf litter and flowering plants.

## Natural history notes

A small hairstreak butterfly characterized by gray-brown undersides crossed by a bold red-orange band, small tail-like extensions on the hindwings, and dark eyespot markings near the tail that can draw predators away from the head. In Florida, it is common in woods, forest edges, hammocks, scrub, gardens, parks, and other areas with leaf litter and flowering plants. Adults feed on nectar from small flowers, while the caterpillars are unusual among butterflies because they feed mainly on fallen dead leaves and other decaying plant material rather than fresh foliage.
